source: manually authored synthetic library workload; not independent real-world sampling
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE lib_readers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL UNIQUE)
CREATE TABLE lib_books(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL UNIQUE, price INTEGER NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE lib_loans(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, reader_id INTEGER NOT NULL, book_id INTEGER NOT NULL, day_no INTEGER NOT NULL, fee INTEGER NOT NULL, returned INTEGER, FOREIGN KEY(reader_id) REFERENCES lib_readers(id), FOREIGN KEY(book_id) REFERENCES lib_books(id))

cases.sql: SELECT r.id FROM lib_readers r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lib_loans l WHERE l.reader_id=r.id) ORDER BY r.id
SELECT r.id,COUNT(l.id) AS n FROM lib_readers r LEFT JOIN lib_loans l ON l.reader_id=r.id GROUP BY r.id ORDER BY r.id
SELECT r.id FROM lib_readers r LEFT JOIN lib_loans l ON l.reader_id=r.id GROUP BY r.id HAVING COALESCE(SUM(l.fee),0)=0 ORDER BY r.id
SELECT reader_id,COUNT(CASE WHEN returned=1 THEN 1 END) AS n FROM lib_loans GROUP BY reader_id ORDER BY reader_id
SELECT DISTINCT r.id FROM lib_readers r JOIN lib_loans l ON l.reader_id=r.id JOIN lib_books b ON b.id=l.book_id WHERE b.price<=20 ORDER BY r.id

cases.intent: Все выдачи в последний день читателя
cases.sql: SELECT l.id,l.reader_id,l.day_no FROM lib_loans l WHERE l.day_no=(SELECT MAX(x.day_no) FROM lib_loans x WHERE x.reader_id=l.reader_id) ORDER BY l.id
SELECT id,price FROM lib_books WHERE price BETWEEN 10 AND 20 ORDER BY id
SELECT id FROM lib_loans WHERE returned<>1 ORDER BY id
SELECT r.id,l.id AS loan_id FROM lib_readers r LEFT JOIN lib_loans l ON l.reader_id=r.id AND l.returned=0 ORDER BY r.id,l.id
SELECT reader_id FROM lib_loans WHERE returned=0 UNION ALL SELECT reader_id FROM lib_loans WHERE fee=0 ORDER BY reader_id

cases.intent: Читатели, у которых все выдачи возвращены
cases.sql: SELECT r.id FROM lib_readers r WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lib_loans l WHERE l.reader_id=r.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lib_loans l WHERE l.reader_id=r.id AND (l.returned<>1 OR l.returned IS NULL)) ORDER BY r.id

cases.intent: Две самые дорогие книги с разрешением равенств
cases.sql: SELECT id,price FROM lib_books ORDER BY price DESC,id ASC LIMIT 2

positive_controls.sql: SELECT id,price FROM lib_books WHERE price>=10 AND price<=20 ORDER BY id
positive_controls.reason: BETWEEN includes both boundaries; non-null integer price.

positive_controls.sql: SELECT id FROM lib_loans WHERE NOT(returned=1) ORDER BY id
positive_controls.reason: Both expressions preserve UNKNOWN for NULL.

positive_controls.sql: SELECT reader_id,COUNT(CASE WHEN returned=1 THEN id END) AS n FROM lib_loans GROUP BY reader_id ORDER BY reader_id
positive_controls.reason: Loan primary key is non-null, preserving conditional count.

positive_controls.sql: SELECT r.id,COUNT(CASE WHEN l.id IS NOT NULL THEN l.id END) AS n FROM lib_readers r LEFT JOIN lib_loans l ON l.reader_id=r.id GROUP BY r.id ORDER BY r.id
positive_controls.reason: Non-null child key counted exactly once per joined child.

comparison: Values including multiplicity and deterministic row order; interfaces separately within each DBMS. NULL only in returned column.
budget: 12 cases x 28 states x 2 DBMS = 672 reference executions; model collection planned only for MySQL (24 responses); no claim of model portability.
